views.name: collisions_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  jurisdiction,
  officer_id,
  reporting_district,
  chp_shift,
  population,
  county_city_location,
  county_location,
  beat_type,
  chp_beat_type,
  beat_number,
  primary_road,
  secondary_road,
  distance,
  direction,
  weather_1,
  weather_2,
  road_surface,
  road_condition_1,
  lighting,
  collision_severity,
  primary_collision_factor,
  type_of_collision,
  hit_and_run,
  tow_away,
  state_route,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  collision_date,
  collision_time,
  process_date,
  killed_victims,
  injured_victims,
  party_count,
  severe_injury_count,
  other_visible_injury_count,
  complaint_of_pain_injury_count,
  pedestrian_killed_count,
  pedestrian_injured_count,
  bicyclist_killed_count,
  bicyclist_injured_count,
  motorcyclist_killed_count,
  motorcyclist_injured_count
FROM collisions
WHERE case_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized projection of collisions with key identifiers, temporal fields cast to canonical types and frequently-used measures exposed. Use this as the cleaned collisions base for joins and aggregations to avoid repeating casts and NULL-safe expressions. | Use for: Time-series or spatial analyses of collisions (by date, county, road, lat/lon).; Filtering collisions by severity, road, weather, or tow_away for downstream joins.

views.name: parties_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  party_type,
  at_fault,
  party_sex,
  party_age,
  party_sobriety,
  party_drug_physical,
  direction_of_travel,
  party_safety_equipment_1,
  party_safety_equipment_2,
  financial_responsibility,
  hazardous_materials,
  cellphone_in_use,
  cellphone_use_type,
  school_bus_related,
  other_associate_factor_1,
  party_number_killed,
  party_number_injured,
  movement_preceding_collision,
  vehicle_year,
  vehicle_make,
  statewide_vehicle_type,
  chp_vehicle_type_towing,
  chp_vehicle_type_towed,
  party_race
FROM parties
WHERE id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Clean projection of parties preserving identifiers and common attributes/flags. Use this as the canonical parties table for joins, party-level filtering, and aggregations. Keeps party id, case link and party_number for safe joins. | Use for: Party-level injury or demographic breakdowns (ages, sex, at-fault counts).; Linking party attributes to collision-level summaries (join on case_id).

views.name: victims_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  victim_role,
  victim_sex,
  victim_age,
  victim_degree_of_injury,
  victim_seating_position,
  victim_safety_equipment_1,
  victim_safety_equipment_2,
  victim_ejected
FROM victims
WHERE id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized projection of victims with identifiers and person-level attributes. Use for victim-level analyses (age, sex, injury) or to aggregate back to collisions. | Use for: Victim demographics and injury-severity summaries.; Joining victims to parties by case_id and party_number to study per-person attributes vs party attributes.

views.name: case_years
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  db_year
FROM case_ids
WHERE case_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Mapping of case_id to db_year from case_ids. Useful to filter or group collisions by source year when joining to collisions. | Use for: Restricting collisions to a particular db_year or comparing counts across db_year values.; Joining collisions to year metadata for temporal reporting.

views.name: parties_by_case_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  COUNT(*) AS party_count_by_partyrows,
  SUM(CASE WHEN at_fault = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS at_fault_count,
  AVG(party_age) AS avg_party_age,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cellphone_in_use = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cellphone_in_use_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(party_number_killed,0)) AS party_number_killed_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(party_number_injured,0)) AS party_number_injured_sum
FROM parties
GROUP BY case_id
views.description: Aggregated party-level measures per collision (case_id). Computes counts and basic summaries useful for collision-level analyses without row proliferation when joining parties to collisions. | Use for: Collision-level aggregates derived from parties (e.g., how many parties were at fault per collision).; Joining these aggregates to collisions to avoid many-to-one duplication.

views.name: victims_by_case_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  COUNT(*) AS victim_count,
  AVG(victim_age) AS avg_victim_age,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'killed' OR victim_degree_of_injury = 'fatal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS killed_count_flagged,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'severe injury' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS severe_injury_count_flagged,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'other visible injury' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS other_visible_injury_count_flagged,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'complaint of pain' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS complaint_of_pain_injury_count_flagged
FROM victims
GROUP BY case_id
views.description: Aggregated victim-level measures per collision (case_id). Provides counts by injury severity and average victim age for collision-level analyses. | Use for: Validate or compare victim-derived injury counts to collisions' aggregated injured/killed columns.; Use victim-level aggregates when collisions' aggregated counts are missing or need cross-checking.

views.name: collisions_with_party_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  c.jurisdiction,
  c.county_location,
  c.primary_road,
  c.collision_date,
  c.collision_time,
  c.killed_victims,
  c.injured_victims,
  c.party_count,
  p.party_count_by_partyrows,
  p.at_fault_count,
  p.avg_party_age,
  p.cellphone_in_use_count,
  p.party_number_killed_sum,
  p.party_number_injured_sum
FROM collisions AS c
LEFT JOIN parties_by_case_agg AS p
  ON c.case_id = p.case_id
views.description: Denormalized collisions joined to aggregated party metrics (one row per collision). Use to combine collision attributes with party-level summaries without inflating rows. | Use for: Assessing collision severity with party-level context (e.g., collisions where many parties were at fault).; Preparing a single-row-per-collision dataset for modeling or reporting.

views.name: party_victim_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.id AS id,
  v.case_id AS case_id,
  v.party_number AS party_number,
  v.victim_role AS victim_role,
  v.victim_sex AS victim_sex,
  v.victim_age AS victim_age,
  v.victim_degree_of_injury AS victim_degree_of_injury,
  p.id AS party_id,
  p.party_type AS party_type,
  p.at_fault AS at_fault,
  p.party_sex AS party_sex,
  p.party_age AS party_age,
  p.vehicle_make AS vehicle_make
FROM victims AS v
LEFT JOIN parties AS p
  ON v.case_id = p.case_id
  AND v.party_number = p.party_number
views.description: Join parties to victims by case_id and party_number to link party attributes to victim attributes. Rows are at the victim (id) grain; use when analyzing person-level outcomes with party context. | Use for: Analyzing how party-level attributes (e.g., at-fault, vehicle_make) correlate with victim injuries.; Creating person-level datasets that include both victim and party fields for logistic modeling.

views.name: collisions_location_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  county_location,
  primary_road,
  COUNT(*) AS collisions_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(killed_victims,0)) AS killed_victims_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(injured_victims,0)) AS injured_victims_sum,
  AVG(COALESCE(party_count,0)) AS avg_party_count
FROM collisions
GROUP BY county_location, primary_road
views.description: Per-location (county_location + primary_road) aggregation of collision counts and summed injury/killed measures. Useful for spatial summaries and ranking locations by harm. | Use for: Which roads/counties have the most collisions or fatalities.; Spatial heatmaps or summarizations by primary road and county.

views.name: collisions_with_db_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  c.collision_date,
  c.county_location,
  c.primary_road,
  c.killed_victims,
  c.injured_victims,
  y.db_year
FROM collisions AS c
LEFT JOIN case_ids AS y
  ON c.case_id = y.case_id
views.description: Collisions enriched with db_year from case_ids, one row per collision. Use to filter or group collisions by the data year source. | Use for: Year-over-year collision trend analyses after grouping by db_year.; Filtering collisions to a specific reporting year via db_year.
